editorial:
Imagine moving into a new house only to find your neighbors are obsessed with Christmas in July, August, and September. That is exactly what happens to Mark and Julie Severson. At first, the Kringles seem like the sweetest, most cheerful people on the block, but things get weird fast. Their son starts spending all his time with them, and you can tell something is off. The movie starts as a funny family story, but it quickly turns into a wild ride with plenty of scares and fight scenes that will keep you on the edge of your seat.

You will love how the movie balances the laughs with the creepy moments. The acting is great, especially the way the Kringles switch from friendly to scary in a heartbeat. While some of the plot twists are a bit predictable, the fast pace makes it easy to enjoy. If you want the best experience, you should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the colorful sets. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great call for future holiday marathons.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the Kringles are actually ancient creatures who feed on holiday cheer and human souls. They tried to kidnap the Severson son to replace their own lost child. After a huge fight in a house filled with deadly ornaments, Mark and Julie manage to burn down the Kringles' home. The movie ends with the family moving away, but the final shot shows a single Christmas light blinking in the ruins, suggesting the monsters survived.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror movies with a funny twist.
